deck: 21 tests across generation, import, search, and annotation tools on the Kugel-Platform image pipeline. Pass/fail per test, minimal commentary.
description: A comprehensive live test matrix of the Kugel-Platform image pipeline: create_agent_artifact_job generation (models, sizes, contexts, edit), import_image_from_url / import_images_from_url, search_images, and the annotation toolset (preview_image_grid, annotate_image elements, check_image_text).

public.body: Every image-related tool on this site's Platform bridge, run once each, live, and published as-is. No cherry-picking — failures are reported exactly like passes.
public.title: What This Is

images.caption: gen_none — no context, fell back to OpenAI

items: gen_header, usageContext=article_header — PASS: routed to fal-ai/flux-2/klein/9b, clean generation.
gen_none, usageContext omitted — PASS but notable: silently fell back to OpenAI gpt-image-1 instead of FAL. This is the real explanation for the earlier '429 no credits' error.
gen_badmodel, model='not-a-real-model-xyz' — correctly rejected: 'Unsupported model for platform'.
gen_text, prompt for a sign reading 'OPEN' — PASS: OCR found legible 'OPEN' baked into the pixels. These models can render some text.
gen_size 1024x768 / 768x1024 / 2048x2048 — all rejected, invalid size enum.
gen_size_portrait (1024x1792) / gen_size_landscape (1792x1024) — both PASS, confirming the real 5-value size allow-list.

gen_edit, operation='edit' — BROKEN: the bridge accepts the field but never forwards sourceArtifact/editMode to pdf-tool. Tried nested-in-requirements and top-level, same failure twice. Genuine gap, not a usage error.
public.title: Generation (create_agent_artifact_job)

items: import_single_baseline (Wikimedia Cat03.jpg) — 429 on the first two attempts (Wikimedia's own rate limit / a bad thumb URL, both unrelated to this platform), then PASS via a Special:FilePath URL: 1600x1598, 280KB.
import_capped (max_bytes=5000, same source) — correctly rejected: 'exceeds import limit (279603 bytes)'. Cap enforcement works as designed.
import_images_from_url batch of 3 URLs — PASS as an async job: 2/3 imported (a coffee/notebook photo, a cosmetic bottle), 1/3 failed 429 (the panorama source, again Wikimedia-side).

import_nonnative (webp from httpbin) — PASS, but stored AS webp. Docs say non-native formats convert to png/jpeg — this one didn't convert. Possible doc/behavior mismatch, or webp counts as native here.
import_badurl — clean 404. Correct behavior, not a bug.
public.title: Import (import_image_from_url / import_images_from_url)

items: search_images, 'modern skincare bottle on a marble countertop' — job completed, 0 candidates. pexels/unsplash/google-cse all skipped for missing API keys; library + openverse found nothing matching. Combined with this site's own maxPaidImports:0 policy, paid image search is fully off right now for two independent reasons, not one.
public.title: Search (search_images)

items: preview_image_grid — PASS: clean 6x6 luminance/busyness grid overlay.
annotate_image scrim element — PASS: bottom gradient scrim + caption text, 0 warnings.
annotate_image logo element — PASS: accepted an artifactRef and rendered without error.
annotate_image device_scale_factor 1 vs 2 — PASS: factor 1 = 750x750px output, factor 2 = 1500x1500px, exactly 4x the pixels as documented.

check_image_text expect_none control on a plain, non-generated stock photo — FALSE POSITIVE: OCR detected 'Li' on a photo with no real text. The warn-only gate has noise even on ordinary photos — a failing expect_none is a prompt to look, not an automatic fail.
public.title: Other Tools (preview_image_grid, annotate_image, check_image_text)

items: No dedicated crop or resize tool exists anywhere on this bridge (confirmed via full tool search). Only the 5-value size enum at generation time and the max_bytes cap at import time control output size. PDF-Tool's own maxDimensionPx downscale param isn't exposed on this bridge.
operation='edit' on create_agent_artifact_job is a declared option with no working implementation through this bridge. Treat image editing as unsupported until it's fixed upstream.
Omitting usageContext doesn't skip model routing — it silently switches provider (FAL to OpenAI). Always set it explicitly, or you're billing the wrong account without knowing it.

search_images' paid providers (pexels/unsplash/google-cse) are listed 'enabled' but have no API keys configured, on top of this site's own maxPaidImports:0 policy. Two independent reasons paid image search returns nothing.
OCR (check_image_text) isn't noise-free even on clean, non-generated photos. A failing expect_none is a signal to look, not an automatic fail.
